## Spatial & Geometric Definition
* Geometry Type: Polyline (Water_Utility_Segment).

* Spatial Delineation: Linear paths of pressurized supply pipes, gravity discharge lines, siphon tubes, and dewatering conduits linking pump stations, wells, and wetland cells.

* Material Typology: High-density polyethylene (HDPE) DR-11/DR-17 pipe, ductile iron pipe (DIP), and reinforced concrete cylinder pipe (RCCP).

### Primary Engineering & Hydraulic Objectives

* Bulk Water Conveyance: Transport large volumes of water (5 to 50+ cfs) between river sources, wells, and isolated interior moist soil units across long distances.

* Pressure Containment: Withstand sustained pumping operating heads, transient hydraulic water hammer surges, and external earth/vehicle loadings.

* Embankment Integrity: Provide closed, continuous conveyance across or through earthen levees without inducing structural piping or seepage along pipe outer walls.

### Technical Specifications & Hydraulic Sizing
* Pipe Diameters: Sized between 12 and 48 in inside diameter based on fluid mechanics equations (Q=V⋅A), restricting internal velocities to 4.0 to 8.0 ft/s to minimize dynamic head loss.

* Pipe Jointing: HDPE pipelines joined using continuous thermal butt-fusion welding per ASTM F2620, producing zero-leakage, fully restrained joint strings.

* Anti-Seepage Measures: Where pipes penetrate through earthen levees, concrete cutoff collars, bentonite seepage rings, and impervious clay backfill are placed along the barrel.

* Siphon Configurations: For over-the-levee pipelines, pipe crowns cross above the levee crest and feature vacuum-breaker valves at the high point to terminate siphon action.

### Quality Control, Inspection & Long-Term Maintenance
* Hydrostatic Pressure Testing: Pressure testing conducted per AWWA standards (e.g., testing at 1.5× working design pressure for 2 hours) prior to trench backfill.

* Internal CCTV Video Inspections: Closed-circuit robotic crawler cameras run through pipe barrels at 5-year intervals to verify the absence of joint displacement, sediment plugs, or internal scaling.

## Spatial Feature Attributes
### Definition
Water Utility Segment: Represents a linear segment of a water distribution system, such as a pipeline or ditch. A subdivision of a wastewater network, particularly a pipeline for the transport of stormwater, sewage or industrial waste between the source, holding facilities, and/or treatment facilities.

### Purpose
Spatial Delineation: Linear paths of pressurized supply pipes, gravity discharge lines, siphon tubes, and dewatering conduits linking pump stations, wells, and wetland cells.

### Applicability
Primary Engineering & Hydraulic Objectives
•	Bulk Water Conveyance: Transport large volumes of water () between river sources, wells, and isolated interior moist soil units across long distances.
•	Pressure Containment: Withstand sustained pumping operating heads, transient hydraulic water hammer surges, and external earth/vehicle loadings.
•	Embankment Integrity: Provide closed, continuous conveyance across or through earthen levees without inducing structural piping or seepage along pipe outer walls.

### Notes
Restoration features now have a Program_UID field to distinguish between NESP and UMRR features. Aliases without program identification will be created for any field that currently has UMRR in the name, so they can be used for NESP or UMRR data.

Attribute criteria for each field includes the following:

* Attribute Status – defines whether the field requires a value or if it is optional based on available information.
* Phases – indicates the earliest time in the project lifecycle values for this attribute as available.
* Digitizing requirements – indicates when the field value should be entered in the attribute table.
Geometry Note: No Z values are needed for this feature.

### WaterUtilitySegment
(line) – A subdivision of a wastewater network, particularly a pipeline for the transport of stormwater, sewage or industrial waste between the source, holding facilities, and/or treatment facilities.

## Parameters

### Program_UID
Designate program NESP or UMRR.

### Project_ID (alias: PROJECT_ID)
Foreign key to the unique NESP/UMRR project ID.

### Type (alias)

### RestorFeatStatus
A description of the status of the individual restoration. It also includes the party responsible for the individual feature.

<table class="table-grid">
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th>Value</th>
      <th>Description</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Planned</td>
      <td>Feature is in a USACE planning stage.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by USACE. If a feature has been planned and built by USACE, once constructed, it will always be considered USACE built even if it has been repaired under later project stages.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature that was not built by USACE has been enhanced by a feature that was USACE built or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>USACE Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that was not built by USACE has been directly improved or repaired.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Planned</td>
      <td>A feature that is planned by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Built</td>
      <td>Feature has been built by another organization or government agency and is an integral part of the UMRR project.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Enhanced</td>
      <td>The function of an existing feature, that was built by another organization or government agency, has been enhanced by a feature that was built or repaired by a non-USACE organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Other Repaired</td>
      <td>An existing feature that has been directly improved or repaired by another organization or government agency.</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

### waterNetworkSubtype
Subtype describing the specific role or classification of the water-related network feature within the restoration project (e.g., distribution line, transmission main, service connection). Used to further categorize water utility network components.

### OperationStatus
Indicates the current operational state of the feature within the water network (e.g., Active, Inactive, Under Construction, Out of Service). Used to distinguish features that are in-service from those that are planned, decommissioned, or temporarily unavailable.

### realPropertySiteUniqueID
Unique identifier for the specific real property site (parcel or facility) associated with the feature. Used to link the feature to site-level real property records.

### realPropertyNetworkUniqueID
Unique identifier for the real property network or system (e.g., a defined utility or infrastructure network) that the feature belongs to. Used to associate individual features with a larger network asset record.

### realPropertyUniqueID
Unique identifier for the individual real property asset represented by the feature. Used to cross-reference the feature with the authoritative real property inventory or asset management system.

### propertyCodeID
Code or identifier representing the property classification or type (e.g., building, utility, easement, parcel). Used for grouping and reporting on property types consistent with real property management standards.

### waterSegmentType
Classification describing the type of water segment represented by the feature (e.g., main channel, side channel, backwater area, intake, outfall). Used to distinguish functional waterbody segments within the project area.

### sdsMetaDataID
References attached metadata.

### RestorFeatIDPK
References attached media.

### sdsID
References attached media.

References attached media.
